title: 'Crypto King' Aiden Pleterski testifies about escape attempt during alleged kidnapping
summary: Self-described "Crypto King" Aiden Pleterski described how he tried to escape and how his alleged kidnappers ultimately released him during his continued testimony at their jury trial in Toronto on…

blocks.text: Toronto·New

Self-described "Crypto King" Aiden Pleterski described how he tried to escape and how his alleged kidnappers ultimately released him during his continued testimony at their jury trial in Toronto on Monday.
Pleterski also recounted threats to his family, beating with golf clubs and his release
'Crypto King’ Aiden Pleterski testifies about alleged 3-day kidnapping ordeal
Pleterski, 27, testified that he was zip-tied and taped to a chair in a "run-down, old home" in the Niagara Region in Ontario on the third and final day of his alleged kidnapping in December 2022.

He also recounted having a COVID-19 mask duct-taped to his face, and more duct tape wrapped around his head and eyes, before he was left in the care of a couple he said told him they'd been paid $5,000 "in dope" to keep him there.
"'What if I can try and convince them I can give them money to let me go?'" Pleterski said in Ontario Superior Court, recounting his thinking at the time.
Pleterski testified this photo was taken of him while he was being held at a home in the Niagara Region during his alleged kidnapping December 2022. (Ontario Superior Court)

Pleterski testified he started telling the couple details from his bankruptcy proceeding, hoping they'd heard of his case, as well as the same "story" he'd told his alleged kidnappers about his former landlord, Sandeep Gupta, hiding money for him.

He said he offered to give the couple $50,000 to $100,000 to release him and would set them up in a hotel downtown Toronto for a few days. Pleterski told the court the couple agreed and rushed him out of the house.

But instead of leaving with them, Pleterski testified he was thrown back into the same Dodge Ram truck he'd been in and out of for three days with his alleged captors. Pleterski said they had a new plan to release him so he could get them money.
"Kid, you're going to go to Sandeep and you're going to get all your assets," Pleterski testified that someone identified as "Slime" told him.
"He said if I don't get money from Sandeep, he's going to kill my family."
"Slime" was the lead kidnapper, according to the Crown, but he is not part of this trial.

Two other men, Alfredo Paladino and Rakeem Henry, who Pleterski testified were also in the truck at that time and part of his kidnapping, are on trial for that and for allegedly extorting and assaulting him.

From left to right, Alfredo Paladino, Akil Heywood and Rakeem Henry are accused of kidnapping and extorting Pleterski in December 2022. (Evan Mitsui/CBC, Instagram/atlanticmastoronto, Evan Mitsui/CBC)

A third man, Akil Heywood, who allegedly invested more than $300,000 with Pleterski and lost a significant amount of it, is also accused of kidnapping and extortion. The Crown described him as the "driving force" behind the plan to kidnap Pleterski.
All three men have pleaded not guilty.
Pleterski was convicted of fraud last month in connection with more than $30 million he took from investors to trade on their behalf, but he has yet to be sentenced.
Released at the Ritz

During their drive back toward Toronto from the Niagara Region, Pleterski said Slime kept oscillating between the plan to let him go to get money from Gupta and giving Pleterski to other groups that wanted him.
"'If they were going to kill me, they would have done it, and if they kill me they won't get money out of me,'" said Pleterski about what he was thinking at the time.
"At this point I'm pleading with him to drop me off with Sandeep."
Pleterski demonstrates how he was grabbed by his alleged kidnappers during his testimony at their jury trial in Toronto last Friday. (Pam Davies/CBC)
Pleterski also testified that the truck stopped at a Walmart along the way. The jury was shown security footage of this.

At the big box store, Pleterski said Paladino purchased a SIM card, which was put in an old iPhone given to Pleterski with two numbers saved in it: one for "John Doe," to communicate with the alleged kidnappers, the other for Gupta.
From there, he said Slime "threw the phone at me" and told him "kid, if you don't do this, your family is going to get smoked."

Crypto King's alleged kidnappers’ trial hears call Aiden Pleterski made to landlord asking for $3M

blocks.text: Pleterski said Slime, Paladino and Henry dropped him off across the street from the Ritz-Carlton in downtown Toronto, where Gupta was living. More security footage was played in court of Pleterski outside the hotel that night.

He phoned Gupta, who he said told him "teams of police" were looking for him. Soon after an officer found him in the lobby of the hotel while Pleterski said he was on the phone with his father telling him he was OK.
Failed meeting

Earlier Monday, Pleterski also described how he was coached to set up a meeting with Gupta at a Tim Hortons in Toronto the previous day, but his alleged captors bailed on the meeting and started heading toward London, Ont.
"When [we] started going toward the highway, my heart sunk a little bit," said Pleterski. "When Slime said there were police there, I felt very scared of what they were going to do to me."
Gupta, testified about the same calls and attempted meeting last week during his own testimony as the Crown's first witness.
Sandeep Gupta, Pleterski's former landlord, testified last week at the trial of three men accused of kidnapping Pleterski. (Pam Davies/CBC)

Pleterski testified about how in London, he was allegedly hit in the face with a pistol and beaten with golf clubs after his alleged kidnappers learned someone he'd convinced them to call had contacted Pleterski's family trying to get money.
When they left the city, Pleterski said his alleged kidnappers appeared to follow a Dodge Durango to the Niagara Region, eventually stopping at the house where Pleterski later tried to escape.

While being led into the house, Pletersi testified that he recognized the voice of another man, who he said was present earlier in his kidnapping when he was forced to record a confession video in the basement of a home in the Pickering area, east of Toronto.
Pleterski is expected to continue his testimony Tuesday morning.
